args.name: Inspect and handle unfamiliar food
args.function: Assess an owned gathered food unit through feasible examination, reporting observable condition, any established food-use knowledge, and uncertainty; allow necessary simple handling such as opening a shell when physically possible.
args.conditions: I own one hazelnut gathered from start-1-nuts at tick 159. A basic observation at tick 160 revealed only local soil conditions, not edibility, shell state, spoilage, or preparation needs. I have not established that this food is safe raw. Three familiar roots remain in reserve.
args.inputs: An owned food unit; any tools or other materials actually required must be specified, not supplied automatically.
args.costs: Method, time, energy, and material requirements are unknown; specify feasible costs and prerequisites.
args.effects: Provide only findings supported by examination or established personal knowledge and explicitly retain uncertainty. If feasible, expose an edible portion through actual handling. Do not guarantee safety, remove toxins, create food, or award wellbeing merely for inspection.

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; tend plots; abandon unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1 energy: dig, then place and cover the unit; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Tend: target a planted plot in reach; one round, 0.5 energy. Abandon: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
candidates.effects: Digging keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It establishes only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 20 rounds, optional checks at 5, 10 and 20; not a growth date. Tend checks the plot and its 0.6 m clearance, kept free of plants by the plant rules; it removes nothing and adds no water, nutrient or growth. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Abandon, or death, before placement returns the unit once (where the person died); a placed unit stays. No reward or refund.

candidates.function: Heat-prepare owned food on an open hearth: clear a bed, light it by hand-drill friction, feed fuel, roast and turn food, inspect, retrieve, smother or cancel.
candidates.costs: Study 3 rounds. Unless stated, a mode takes 1 round. prepare-hearth: x,y in reach on dry open ground 0.7 m clear of objects, loose items and people; 2 paid rounds of 1 energy clear a 0.45 m bed, no stock. tend: inputs owned branch, bark or dry-grass in tenths (bed holds 8 mass) and/or turn:true; 0.5 energy. ignite: unlit hearth loaded with dry-grass 0.5 and branch 0.5; board one owned branch or willow, spindle one owned harder birch or oak; up to 12 drilling rounds of 1.5 energy, then ember transfer and first tending at 0.5 each; repeat ignite to continue. cook: inputs one whole owned root or berry (quantity 1); 0.5 energy. inspect: target, or up to 4 inputs; 0.2 energy. retrieve or extinguish: 0.5 energy. cancel: no energy. Gather and travel cost extra.
candidates.effects: Fuel and wood moisture starts at current rain, +0.08*rain per rainy round, else -0.01*(1+wind). Drilling wears a socket and makes dust; an ember forms only when 2 g of dust reaches 350 C (20 W drill; wind cools, moisture cuts, none above 0.35; warms with consecutive rounds), else the trial fails after 12 rounds, leaving worn pieces and dust. Drilling and transfer need rain<=0.15, wind<=0.65, fuel moisture<=0.35; an unworked ember dies. A lit fire burns at most 1 fuel unit per round times dryness (10% ash), keeps embers 3 rounds, is doused by rain>0.6 and catches loose fuel on its rim. Heat: 2 MJ per fuel unit, 18 minutes per round (heat only); the bed stores and loses heat; food on it heats from below, loses water at 100 C and chars above 200 C once dry. Cooked: core 85 C for 10 minutes; charred: 20% of solids burnt. Handling on a bed over 60 C or food over 50 C needs an owned branch as a stick; raked-aside food cools. Retrieved food keeps its age and spoilage and eats as one unit at its original nutrition times its unburnt solids share; char stays as residue. No detoxification, preservation, warmth or reward. Inspect records perceivable state and a model estimate, not core temperature.
